The SRMR With Its Unbiased Estimate, Confidence Interval, and Tests of Fit

Source: R/sem_residual_fit.R
sem_residual_fit.Rd

Summarizes how far a fitted model's implied covariances are from the observed ones with the standardized root mean square residual (SRMR) and gives it the inferential treatment the RMSEA has long had: the asymptotically unbiased estimate of the population SRMR of Maydeu-Olivares (2017), its standard error and confidence interval, a test of exact fit, and an optional test of close fit, together with the largest standardized residual. The SRMR is an effect size of misfit in the metric of a correlation, and Maydeu-Olivares, Shi, and Rosseel (2018) found its interval and test of close fit more accurate than those of the RMSEA in models with many variables. The computations are lavaan's (lavaan::lavResiduals()), and the function requires lavaan 0.7-2 or newer (in Suggests).

Usage

sem_residual_fit(fit, conf_level = 0.9, close_fit = NULL)

Arguments

fit

A fitted lavaan model: a maximum likelihood fit (estimator ML, MLM, MLMV, or MLR) under lavaan's default normal likelihood, of one group of continuous variables at a single level, from complete raw data (fitted under listwise deletion, FIML, or pairwise deletion) or from a covariance matrix. It must have converged to an admissible solution, as sem_fit_measures judges it. See Details for what is refused and why.

conf_level

Confidence level of the interval for the population SRMR. Defaults to 0.90, as lavaan's does and as every RMSEA interval in DMAR does: a 90 percent interval pairs with a test of close fit at .05 (see Details). conf_level = 0.95 gives a 95 percent interval.

close_fit

Optional bound \(c\) for the test of close fit, \(H_0: \mathrm{SRMR} \le c\). Without it, no bound is imposed and the close_fit_bound and p_close_fit rows are NA. There is no universal value: Maydeu-Olivares, Shi, and Rosseel (2018) treat the bound as the researcher's choice. Shi, Maydeu-Olivares, and DiStefano (2018) proposed population reference values that scale with the average \(R^2\) (communality) of the observed variables, in a criterion with two parts that must both hold: a model fits closely when its SRMR is at most .05 times the average \(R^2\) and its largest absolute standardized residual covariance is at most .10 (and acceptably at .10 times the average \(R^2\) and .15). They recommend applying these population values through an interval or a test of close fit rather than to the sample values, so close_fit = 0.05 times the average \(R^2\) tests the first part (lavaan::lavInspect(fit, "rsquare") gives the \(R^2\) values). The second part is not tested here; the row largest_absolute_residual is its sample value, which they caution against comparing with .10 unless the sample is very large. Ximénez, Maydeu-Olivares, Shi, and Revuelta (2022) found the bound of the first part, applied to the unbiased SRMR, to work reasonably well in finite samples, except that with small loadings (an average \(R^2\) of .09) close fit called for samples of 500 or more, and recommend it.

Value

A dmar_tbl (class dmar_sem_fit) with columns term and value and, always in this order, the rows srmr (the sample SRMR), srmr_se_exact_fit (its standard error under exact fit only), p_exact_fit, unbiased_srmr, unbiased_srmr_se, unbiased_srmr_ci_lower, unbiased_srmr_ci_upper, close_fit_bound and p_close_fit (NA unless close_fit is given), srmr_mean (NA without a mean structure), largest_absolute_residual, and N. Attributes: standardized_residuals, the matrix of standardized covariance residuals; largest_residual, the pair of variables with the largest absolute residual and its signed value; and sem_fit, which records the residual covariance, the information setting, the cases used, and the lines of the printed footer.

Details

The SRMR and Its Unbiased Estimate

With \(p\) observed variables, sample covariances \(s_{ij}\), and model implied covariances \(\hat{\sigma}_{ij}\), the standardized residuals are \(e_{ij} = (s_{ij} - \hat{\sigma}_{ij}) / \sqrt{s_{ii} s_{jj}}\), and the SRMR is \(\sqrt{\sum_{i \le j} e_{ij}^2 / t}\) over the \(t = p(p + 1)/2\) variances and covariances (row srmr; lavaan's srmr_bentler_nomean). Its population counterpart is the same quantity computed from the population covariances, a measure of the size of misfit that does not depend on the sample size. The sample SRMR overestimates it, since sampling error adds to every residual. Maydeu-Olivares (2017) removes the bias on the squared scale: with \(\Xi\) the asymptotic covariance matrix of the standardized residuals and \(e\) their vector, the unbiased estimate (row unbiased_srmr) is \(k^{-1}\sqrt{\max(e'e - \mathrm{tr}\,\Xi, 0)/t}\), with \(k = 1 - [\mathrm{tr}(\Xi^2) + 2e'\Xi e]/[4(e'e)^2]\) (Maydeu-Olivares et al., 2018, Eq. 16). It is truncated at zero when the estimated sampling contribution exceeds \(e'e\), and the square root and the truncation leave some bias in small samples.

The Interval and the Test of Close Fit

The interval for the population SRMR is the large sample normal reference interval \(\hat{\rho}_u \pm z_{1 - \alpha/2} \widehat{SE}(\hat{\rho}_u)\) for the unbiased estimate \(\hat{\rho}_u\) (Maydeu-Olivares et al., 2018, Eqs. 20 and 22), where \(\alpha\) is 1 minus conf_level. Its limits are reported as lavaan returns them, without truncation, so the lower limit can fall below zero although the population SRMR cannot, and when the estimate is truncated to zero the interval is centered at zero. In the simulations of Maydeu-Olivares et al. (2018) the interval computed without the normality assumption covered at close to the nominal rate in most conditions, including models of 60 variables, and did less well than the RMSEA interval only for very small misfit in small models, and then mostly in small samples; computed under normality, it covered poorly when the data were not normal. The test of close fit, \(H_0: \mathrm{SRMR} \le c\), refers \(z = (\hat{\rho}_u - c)/\widehat{SE}(\hat{\rho}_u)\) to the standard normal (Maydeu-Olivares et al., 2018, Eq. 21; row p_close_fit); it rejects at level \(\alpha\) exactly when the lower limit of the \(100(1 - 2\alpha)\) percent interval exceeds \(c\), so the default conf_level = 0.90 pairs with a test at .05, as the RMSEA interval of sem_fit_measures does with its tests, and conf_level = 0.95 with a test at .025. The printed table states the level beneath it. Failing to reject close fit does not establish it.

The Test of Exact Fit

The test of exact fit (row p_exact_fit) asks whether the population SRMR is zero. It uses the sample (biased) SRMR, whose expected value and standard error under exact fit are known (Maydeu-Olivares, 2017): \(z = \max(\mathrm{SRMR} - E_0, 0) / SE_0\), referred to the upper tail of the standard normal. The row srmr_se_exact_fit is that standard error, \(SE_0 = \sqrt{\mathrm{tr}(\Xi^2)/(2t\,\mathrm{tr}\,\Xi)}\), which holds only under exact fit: it is not the standard error of the sample SRMR of a misspecified model and must not be used to form an interval, which is what the unbiased estimate and its standard error are for. Because of the truncation at zero the p-value is at most 0.5, and it equals 0.5 whenever the sample SRMR is below its expectation under exact fit, as it is more than half the time when the model is correct.

Which Fits, and the Residual Covariance

The asymptotic covariance \(\Xi\) of the residuals, and so the unbiased estimate, its standard error, the interval, and both tests, depend on the fit, as lavaan computes them. For an ML fit with standard errors under normality it is normal theory. When the fit computed the asymptotic covariance matrix of the sample moments from their fourth order moments (MLM, MLMV, or a Satorra-Bentler test), or uses sandwich standard errors (MLR), it is asymptotically distribution free, which is the version to use with nonnormal item data, for which normal theory intervals perform poorly (Maydeu-Olivares et al., 2018). The projection onto the residual space uses the fit's information setting, so observed information (the default under MLR) gives slightly different values from expected information; an MLR fit with information = "expected" reproduces MLM. The standardizing standard deviations are treated as fixed. The sem_fit attribute records which residual covariance and information were used.

The function refuses what these computations do not cover, each with a message that says why: estimators other than ML (least squares and categorical estimators), likelihood = "wishart", multiple groups, multilevel models, ordered variables, sampling weights, conditional.x = TRUE (whose residuals are conditional on the exogenous covariates rather than the marginal covariances the SRMR summarizes), fits with incomplete data under FIML or pairwise deletion, and two-stage fits. A FIML or pairwise fit of data with no missing values is accepted: its residuals, their standard errors, and the tests are those of a listwise fit with the same mean structure and information setting (FIML's default is the observed information, which the footer names). A fit with auxiliary variables (lavaan's aux) is refused: lavaan's residual summary averages over them, and their residuals of about zero lower the SRMR, while with complete data they change nothing in the model's fit, so the fit without them is the one to summarize. A fit whose cases were removed by listwise deletion is evaluated on the complete cases with a warning, since that assumes the data are missing completely at random. A model fitted from a covariance matrix (sample.cov) gives the same values as one fitted to the raw data under normal theory, since these need only the moments. For a saturated model (zero degrees of freedom) the residuals are zero up to the convergence tolerance, and the standard errors, limits, and p-values are NA, with a warning that says so.

The SRMR here summarizes the covariance residuals only. For a model with a mean structure, row srmr_mean is the root mean square of the standardized mean residuals, zero when the means are saturated; when the model restricts the means, a warning points to it, since the covariance SRMR does not reflect misfit in the means. Always look at the residuals themselves as well as their average (the attribute standardized_residuals): a good average can hide a large local misfit.

References

Maydeu-Olivares, A. (2017). Assessing the size of model misfit in structural equation models. Psychometrika, 82(3), 533–558. doi:10.1007/s11336-016-9552-7

Maydeu-Olivares, A., Shi, D., & Rosseel, Y. (2018). Assessing fit in structural equation models: A Monte-Carlo evaluation of RMSEA versus SRMR confidence intervals and tests of close fit. Structural Equation Modeling, 25(3), 389–402. doi:10.1080/10705511.2017.1389611

Shi, D., Maydeu-Olivares, A., & DiStefano, C. (2018). The relationship between the standardized root mean square residual and model misspecification in factor analysis models. Multivariate Behavioral Research, 53(5), 676–694. doi:10.1080/00273171.2018.1476221

Ximénez, C., Maydeu-Olivares, A., Shi, D., & Revuelta, J. (2022). Assessing cutoff values of SEM fit indices: Advantages of the unbiased SRMR index and its cutoff criterion based on communality. Structural Equation Modeling, 29(3), 368–380. doi:10.1080/10705511.2021.1992596

See also

sem_fit_measures for the chi square, RMSEA, and incremental indices beside the sample SRMR, and equivalence_rmsea for the test of not close fit of the RMSEA.

Examples

# The three-factor model of nine holzinger_swineford tests.
fit <- lavaan::cfa(
  "visual  =~ t1_visual_perception + t2_cubes + t4_lozenges
   textual =~ t6_paragraph_comprehension + t7_sentence + t9_word_meaning
   speed   =~ t10_addition + t12_counting_groups_of_dots +
              t13_straight_and_curved_capitals",
  data = holzinger_swineford, std.lv = TRUE)
sem_residual_fit(fit)
#>  term                      value   
#>  srmr                      0.065   
#>  srmr_se_exact_fit         0.006   
#>  p_exact_fit               < 0.0001
#>  unbiased_srmr             0.058   
#>  unbiased_srmr_se          0.010   
#>  unbiased_srmr_ci_lower    0.042   
#>  unbiased_srmr_ci_upper    0.074   
#>  close_fit_bound           <NA>    
#>  p_close_fit               <NA>    
#>  srmr_mean                 <NA>    
#>  largest_absolute_residual 0.189   
#>  N                         301     
#> 
#> Confidence level: 90%
#> 
#> Residual covariance: normal theory; expected information
#> Largest standardized residual: t2_cubes with t10_addition, -0.189

# The 90 percent interval, the default, pairs with a test of close fit
# at .05. The bound is the researcher's choice; here it is .05 times the
# average R squared of the nine tests, the population value for close
# fit of Shi, Maydeu-Olivares, and DiStefano (2018).
r2 <- lavaan::lavInspect(fit, "rsquare")
sem_residual_fit(fit, close_fit = 0.05 * mean(r2))
#>  term                      value   
#>  srmr                      0.065   
#>  srmr_se_exact_fit         0.006   
#>  p_exact_fit               < 0.0001
#>  unbiased_srmr             0.058   
#>  unbiased_srmr_se          0.010   
#>  unbiased_srmr_ci_lower    0.042   
#>  unbiased_srmr_ci_upper    0.074   
#>  close_fit_bound           0.025   
#>  p_close_fit               0.0003  
#>  srmr_mean                 <NA>    
#>  largest_absolute_residual 0.189   
#>  N                         301     
#> 
#> Confidence level: 90%
#> 
#> Residual covariance: normal theory; expected information
#> Largest standardized residual: t2_cubes with t10_addition, -0.189

# A 95 percent interval instead.
sem_residual_fit(fit, conf_level = 0.95)
#>  term                      value   
#>  srmr                      0.065   
#>  srmr_se_exact_fit         0.006   
#>  p_exact_fit               < 0.0001
#>  unbiased_srmr             0.058   
#>  unbiased_srmr_se          0.010   
#>  unbiased_srmr_ci_lower    0.039   
#>  unbiased_srmr_ci_upper    0.077   
#>  close_fit_bound           <NA>    
#>  p_close_fit               <NA>    
#>  srmr_mean                 <NA>    
#>  largest_absolute_residual 0.189   
#>  N                         301     
#> 
#> Confidence level: 95%
#> 
#> Residual covariance: normal theory; expected information
#> Largest standardized residual: t2_cubes with t10_addition, -0.189
